reviewEvidence: Two-pass review of revision-078eb341 (head b520a3a for the hash; reviewed at head 738f2b6 with no task-owned path changes since the seal). PASS 1 (verify phase) re-checked every acceptance criterion against the code: the setup install writes exactly one record per attempt and the audit writer redacts the new `errorSummary` (`src/audit.ts:31`); `combineCommandOutput` feeds `formatToolOutput` so the displayed text, the truncation tail and the persisted copy all carry both streams; both timeout schemas now declare `exclusiveMinimum: 0` and the tests compile them the way Pi validates tool arguments; `authorize()` runs at `src/execution-service.ts:140`, before the audited bind block at :155, so `policyAuthorized: true` on a refusal record is truthful; the discovery sink dedupes, is fed by the same `registry()` function that `refreshRegistry` points at, and reports only through `ctx.ui.notify`; both RED reproductions were produced by stashing source only. PASS 2 (this phase) was an INDEPENDENT adversarial review by a fresh-context agent with no memory of the implementation, instructed to falsify the two strongest claims ("exactly one setup record on every path", "no structured execution path drops stderr any more"), to check each AC against code rather than tests, to hunt regressions from the two deleted registry fields, and to run the security profile. It confirmed: no dependency changes in either commit; the installer still runs the fixed `SETUP_ARGV` with the interactive confirm and `hasUI` gate unchanged; the audit redaction covers the new failure paths; diagnostics reach only the operator UI and never model context; and the regression sweep found no remaining `configOnly`/`orphanDockerCandidates`/`hostCommandIdentity` consumer in code, docs, tests or `dist/` (the identifiers survive only in historical artifacts and the CHANGELOG), with `dist/` containing the new symbols. Its verdict: AC-1..AC-5 satisfied as literally worded and AC-6 verified for typecheck, the 326-test suite, `install:local --check` and dist parity (it could not independently re-run the packed smoke because that script rewrites `dist/`). It did falsify the broader "no path drops stderr" claim and surfaced eight further gaps; every concrete claim was re-verified against the source before being recorded here (commands.ts ternary, `grep -c onStderr src/runtime/docker-lifecycle.ts` = 0, the `Math.round` at tools.ts:123, `grep -rn discoveryDiagnostics tests/` = 0, the shipped README.zh-CN table, and the stale tool-output.ts comment). No blocking finding: AC-2's wording scopes it to `devcontainer_exec`, and the two remaining stderr-dropping surfaces plus the other minor gaps are pre-existing behaviour on surfaces outside this revision's scope — they are recorded for a scoped follow-up rather than silently accepted.

findings.message: Pre-existing, but it defeats this phase's goal in the field: `toSpawnError` handles `ENOENT` and `EACCES`/`EPERM` and maps every other errno to `unexpected` with the message `Failed to spawn: <file>`, dropping `cause.code`. Observed on 2026-09-15: a host-wide `ENOTCONN` condition (a dead Orca AppImage FUSE mount occupying PATH ahead of the real binaries, which makes glibc `execvp` abort the whole search) rendered as exactly the same opaque text as a missing binary, sending diagnosis toward "the devcontainer CLI is not installed" while `devcontainer --version` reported 0.89.0 and the container was up. Include the errno in the message and remedy, and consider naming ENOTCONN explicitly as a host-environment fault. Scheduled as a follow-up tweak.

Found by the independent pass; AC-2 as worded is satisfied (it names `devcontainer_exec`, and the host TOOL was fixed with it), but the L2-02 class is not closed repo-wide. (a) `src/commands.ts:543` — the `/devcontainer host-exec` slash command still runs the exact ternary this revision deleted elsewhere (`result.stdout.length > 0 ? result.stdout : result.stderr.length > 0 ? result.stderr : ...`), so the host escape hatch loses stderr through the command surface even though the tool surface no longer does. (b) `src/runtime/docker-lifecycle.ts` — `logs()` passes only `onData` (`grep -c onStderr` on that file = 0) and `destructive()` (stop/remove) captures neither stream and reports only the exit code, so `docker logs`' stderr half and all stop/remove diagnostics are discarded. Fix with the same `combineCommandOutput` helper; both are worth folding into the follow-up tweak or Phase 5.

Found by the independent pass. `src/tools.ts:123` computes `Math.round(params.timeoutSeconds * 1000)`, so a positive-but-sub-millisecond value (e.g. `0.0004`) still becomes `setTimeout(..., 0)` and reproduces the exact immediate-abort failure the schema change was meant to prevent. The schema cannot express a millisecond floor; either reject values below 0.001 or compute `Math.max(1, Math.round(...))`. Related and also unaddressed: the routed `bash` tool takes Pi's own unbounded `timeout` (no minimum in Pi's schema) and passes `0`/negatives straight into the same immediate abort (`src/bash-router.ts`).

Found by the independent pass. `src/setup-cli.ts` writes its record and then branches on `runResult.exitCode !== 0`; when the child is signal-killed the runner resolves with `exitCode: null`, so the structured result becomes `error: "npm install exited null"` — an unhelpful message that also discards `runResult.signal`, which is the only field that says what happened. Record the signal in the audit record and name it in the error.

Found by the independent pass. The `setup` record is written for the install stage before the verification probe runs, so a failed probe leaves an audit record with `exitCode: 0` and no `errorSummary` while the operator is told `[setup-failed] …`. The design said "one attempt = exactly one `setup` record, whatever stage fails", which this contradicts for the probe stage, and a judge reading the record alone would conclude setup succeeded. Either write the record after the probe (carrying the probe failure in `errorSummary`) or keep one record per stage with an explicit stage field.

Found by the independent pass. `writeRecord` calls `deps.audit.write` unguarded, and the writer does `mkdirSync`/`appendFileSync` with no error handling, so an audit failure (read-only state dir, disk full, permissions) throws out of the setup path unnormalized while producing no record at all — the one case where "exactly one record" cannot hold. A `try`/`catch` around the write that still returns the structured `{installed:false, error}` would keep the contract honest.

Found by the independent pass and confirmed (`grep -rn discoveryDiagnostics tests/` = 0 matches): nothing tests the operator-facing half of AC-5. Deleting the drain-and-notify block at `extensions/index.ts:673` leaves the suite green at 326/326, because only the sink itself is unit-tested, not its wiring into the command dispatch. AC-5's claim is "surfaced to the operator", so the missing seam is exactly the one the AC is about — stub `ctx.ui.notify` and assert a queued diagnostic is drained and reported (and that a second identical pass reports nothing).

Found by the independent pass. The audit copy of an install failure is redacted (`src/audit.ts:31`), but the string returned as `error` is raw npm stderr — and that value is both shown to the operator and handed to the model as the command result, so a registry token echoed by npm (`npm ERR! ... _authToken=...`) would land in model context even though the trail is clean. Pass it through `redactText` before returning.

Found by the independent pass and confirmed: `README.zh-CN.md:161,163` still documents `timeoutSeconds` without the new "must be positive" contract, and that file IS shipped (`package.json` `files` includes `README.zh-CN.md`), so the two READMEs now disagree. Additionally `src/tool-output.ts:61` still documents `@param output combined stdout (callers choose stdout-or-stderr precedence)` — stale twice over, since callers now pass the combined output produced by `combineCommandOutput`.

Found by the independent pass. Four assertions in `tests/unit/host-discovery.test.ts` were rewritten from `expect(result.configOnly/orphanDockerCandidates)...` to `expect(result.diagnostics).toEqual([])`, which asserts nothing about the fields that were removed — they would pass against the pre-change code too. The removal itself is covered by the `Object.keys(result)` boundary test, so this is test hygiene rather than a coverage hole, but the four lines should assert something real (e.g. that the orphan candidate still appears as a `docker-label` entry) or be deleted.

The newly surfaced diagnostics include host filesystem paths (`cannot read directory <dir>`, `max depth N reached; not traversing <dir>`, `not traversing <dir>: resolves outside allowed workspace root`). The disclosure is bounded and deliberate: the lines go to the operator's UI only, never into the model context and never into the audit file, and the same paths are already visible through `/devcontainer list`. If a future change routes these into model context, this must be revisited.

The drain sits immediately after `await handler(...)`, so a verb handler that throws leaves its diagnostics queued until the next successful `/devcontainer` command. Nothing is lost (the sink keeps pending lines) but a failure-path diagnostic is delivered one command late; a `finally` would report it immediately.

The host resolves the Dev Containers CLI at 0.89.0 while the architecture review's host-contract constraints were recorded against 0.88.0 (argv shape and exit-code semantics for `up`/`build`/`exec`). Nothing in this revision depends on the difference and both the packed smoke run and a real `devcontainer exec --workspace-folder <ws> -- echo alive` succeed against the installed version, but the documented contract should be re-confirmed at 0.89.0 in the next phase.
